oneLine: Bitcoin and Ethereum fell 2.1–2.5% on Sept 23 after US Treasury yields spiked to a 19-year high on strong economic data, triggering $280 million in liquidations and closing BitMEX permanently at 04:00 UTC.
caveman: Bitcoin and Ethereum both dropped about 2% on September 23 because the US economy looked stronger than everyone expected. When the US government's borrowing costs go up (the 10-year Treasury yield jumped to 5.1%), people move money away from Bitcoin to earn that higher interest. A big Bitcoin trading platform called BitMEX also shut down completely at 04:00 UTC that day—it had been running for 11 years. A lot of people who had borrowed money to bet on higher prices got forced to sell (we call this liquidation), which pushed prices down further. The overall feeling in the market stayed calm ('Greed'), but it was still a worrying day because of all the selling.
priceVolumeSummary: All five major exchanges—Binance, OKX, Bybit, Bitget, and Gate—quoted Bitcoin within $2 of $84,210, showing strong price agreement. Binance dominated volume at $17.8 billion, far ahead of OKX ($8.4B) and Gate ($7.8B).
positioningSummary: Traders paid positive interest (4–10.95% annualized) betting on price gains, but open interest shrank 2–9.6% as positions closed. Long-to-short ratios stayed bullish (Bitcoin 1.16:1 on Binance, Ethereum 2.78:1), yet liquidations hit $280 million in Bitcoin longs as the price break below $84,000 squeezed leveraged bulls.
stocksSummary: Asian markets fell on Sept 23 as Treasury yields soared: Korea's KOSPI down 1.75%, Hong Kong's Zhipu AI down 10.9%, China's CXMT down 2.5%. US equities declined in lockstep (S&P 500 −0.72%, Nasdaq −1.10%). Gold gained +0.12% as investors sought safe havens.

topThree.headline: BitMEX ends 11-year run with permanent trading shutdown
topThree.what: BitMEX, the pioneer exchange that introduced 100x leverage, ceased all trading at 04:00 UTC Sept 23 and is winding down. Positions were force-closed automatically. Users must withdraw remaining funds; fees now apply to balances left on the platform.

topThree.headline: US Treasury yield surges to 5.1%, highest since 2007, on strong PMI data
topThree.what: The 10-year Treasury yield spiked 18 basis points on Sept 23 after Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) reports showed unexpected economic strength: Services PMI 58.7 (best in 5 years), Manufacturing PMI 56.7 (best in 4 years). The move flushed leveraged positions across crypto and stocks.
topThree.timeUTC: Throughout Sept 23 (yields peaked mid-day US Eastern)

topThree.headline: Bitcoin long liquidations hit $280 million as price dips below $84,000
topThree.what: As the 10-year Treasury yield spiked, Bitcoin fell below $84,000 and triggered cascade liquidations of leveraged long positions. Cointelegraph reported $280 million in BTC long closures as the price break forced automated sell-offs.
topThree.timeUTC: Sept 23, intraday (timestamps 17:51–18:51 UTC range in sources)

Exchange and platform changes.headline: Kalshi prediction market says CFTC has not contacted it over $5B trading activity
Exchange and platform changes.what: Kalshi responded to scrutiny over unusual Ether perpetual trades valued at nearly $5 billion, saying the CFTC has not contacted it and attributing the activity to its liquidity incentive programs. The platform rejected wash-trading allegations.

Exchange and platform changes.headline: Hut 8 wins $140 million bid for Poolin's Texas Bitcoin mining data centers
Exchange and platform changes.what: Hut 8 acquired Poolin's two Texas locations in a competitive bid, expanding its data-center footprint for both Bitcoin mining and AI compute. The deal underscores institutional focus on infrastructure as mining profitability shifts.

Institutional flows and ETFs.headline: Bitcoin ETFs net $104M outflow; Ethereum nets $162M inflow on Sept 23
Institutional flows and ETFs.what: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a rare $104 million net outflow on Sept 23, as the Treasury yield spike and price break spooked some investors. Ethereum ETFs bucked the trend with $162.2 million inflow—their third straight day of net buying.

Institutional flows and ETFs.headline: Bitcoin and Ethereum options worth $15.6–$18 billion expire Friday; call-heavy book
Institutional flows and ETFs.what: Nearly $18 billion in combined Bitcoin and Ethereum options expiring Sept 25 (Friday) create potential dealer hedging flows and volatility. Deribit's data shows a call-heavy book, with positions stacked at multiple strikes.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Nearly $20 million in XRP stolen from 6,678 wallets across six attack waves
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: XRPL.to documented six separate compromise waves draining almost $20 million in XRP from thousands of wallets through Sept 20. DCENT (wallet maker) advised users to replace exposed recovery phrases immediately, even on hardware wallets.

Regulation and policy.headline: SEC Commissioner Uyeda: agency dropped crypto cases to avoid credibility issues in court
Regulation and policy.what: Former SEC acting chair Mark Uyeda disclosed that the SEC dropped many cases against crypto companies in early 2025 to sidestep potential court defeats that could damage the agency's credibility. The admission signals a policy shift toward lighter enforcement.

Regulation and policy.headline: Senate Banking Committee Democrats call for public hearing on prediction markets
Regulation and policy.what: All Democrats on the Senate Banking Committee urged Chair Tim Scott to hold a congressional hearing on prediction markets, amid separate Republican private meetings with Kalshi. The move signals Democratic interest in regulatory oversight of the sector.

Product launches and partnerships.headline: Circle launches 24/7 stablecoin FX trading engine for USDC and other pairs
Product launches and partnerships.what: Circle introduced a fully-automated foreign-exchange engine for stablecoins, offering 24/7 settlement of supported pairs (e.g. USDC, EUROC). Screened firms can participate; local fiat access and custody require separate arrangements.

Product launches and partnerships.headline: Coinbase expands Morpho Protocol integration: fixed-rate Bitcoin loans now live
Product launches and partnerships.what: Coinbase users can now borrow USDC against Bitcoin at a locked-in rate and repayment date via Morpho Midnight. This marks the first enterprise-scale deployment of Morpho Midnight and a shift from volatile on-chain lending rates.

Product launches and partnerships.headline: Canada's big six banks jointly explore tokenized-deposit system for settlements
Product launches and partnerships.what: RBC, TD, BMO, Scotiabank, CIBC, and National Bank announced a collaborative project to build a shared Canadian-dollar tokenized-deposit network. Phase one focuses on interbank transfers; fiat on/off-ramps follow later.

Product launches and partnerships.headline: NYSE and Blockchain.com plan tokenized US stock trading platform
Product launches and partnerships.what: The New York Stock Exchange and Blockchain.com signed an agreement to explore a digital-asset trading platform for tokenized US stocks and ETFs, pending regulatory approval. The move accelerates Wall Street's pivot to on-chain trading.

Product launches and partnerships.headline: MoonPay acquires SEC-registered North Capital in $60 million all-stock deal
Product launches and partnerships.what: MoonPay bought North Capital, an SEC-registered broker-dealer, to accelerate its tokenized real-world assets (RWA) ambitions. CEO Ivan Soto-Wright cited mass adoption of tokenized assets as the rationale.

Unconfirmed and watch items.headline: CONTEXT: Kalshi $5 billion in Ether perps drew attention but no formal investigation (Sept 22)
Unconfirmed and watch items.what: Separately from today's statement, Kalshi disclosed unusual trading patterns in its Ether perpetuals—nearly $5 billion in similarly-sized trades. The platform attributed the volume to liquidity incentive programs and said the CFTC has not formally opened an investigation.

Unconfirmed and watch items.headline: BlackRock sees $5 trillion AI-driven stablecoin market emerging
Unconfirmed and watch items.what: BlackRock research suggests autonomous AI systems could create a new class of stablecoin customers—machines that spend continuously without human approval. The asset manager anticipates this AI-to-AI commerce could unlock a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity.

Unconfirmed and watch items.headline: Visa study: stablecoin adoption intent jumps to 56% with bank-level protections
Unconfirmed and watch items.what: A Visa survey found US adoption intent for stablecoins rises from 36% to 56% if they carry FDIC-like deposit insurance. The finding signals demand for regulatory clarity and consumer protections ahead of the GENIUS Act.

etfFlows.summary: Bitcoin spot ETFs saw $104 million in net outflows as the Treasury yield spike and price break spooked some investors. Ethereum spot ETFs bucked the trend with $162.2 million in inflows, marking the third consecutive day of net buying despite the broader market sell-off.

calendarNotes.event: SNB and Riksbank rate decisions (Sept 24, 07:30 UTC), Norges Bank rate decision (Sept 24, 08:00 UTC)
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: European central-bank decisions can shift appetite for risk assets; hawkish surprises may extend the yield rally and hurt crypto.
High claims (layoffs) would ease Fed rate-hike odds; low claims would reinforce labor-market strength and support higher Treasury yields.
Australian central-bank move could influence global risk sentiment and commodity/currency flows.

calendarNotes.event: US Non-Farm Payrolls (Oct 2, 12:30 UTC) — high impact
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: Major jobs report; strong employment could accelerate rate-hike bets and extend the yield rally, pressuring crypto.

glossary.definition: A unit equal to 1/100th of 1 percent. When the 10-year Treasury yield rose 18 basis points, it rose 0.18 percentage points (e.g., from 4.92% to 5.10%).
A fund that trades on an exchange like a stock. Bitcoin and Ethereum spot ETFs track the price of those coins and let investors buy exposure without owning the actual coins.
Inflow = net buying into an ETF; outflow = net selling. Positive inflow means more people bought than sold; negative outflow means more sold than bought.

Interest paid by traders betting on price increases to traders betting on price decreases, or vice versa. Positive funding means bulls are paying bears, signaling strong bullish sentiment. Paid every 8 hours on major exchanges.

Forced automatic sale of a leveraged position when the price moves against it and the margin runs out. Example: a trader who borrowed money to bet on Bitcoin rising gets forced to sell if the price falls too fast.
A bet that the price will go up. Opposite of short (a bet that price will go down).
The ratio of bullish (long) positions to bearish (short) positions. A ratio of 1.16:1 means 16% more bullish bets than bearish ones.
The price used to calculate gains/losses and margin requirements on futures and perpetuals. It tracks the spot price closely to prevent manipulation.
The total number of open (unsettled) contracts on an exchange. When open interest falls, it means positions are being closed; when it rises, new positions are being opened.
The day's percentage gain or loss in total open positions. Negative change (e.g., −9.6%) means traders closed positions net; positive change means they opened them.
Contracts that let traders bet on price movements without owning the underlying coin. Perpetuals never expire; futures expire on a set date. Both use leverage (borrowed money).
A survey-based measure of business activity in manufacturing and services. Readings above 50 signal expansion; 58.7 (services) is very strong and typically triggers fears of higher interest rates.

A loan you make to the US government; the 10-year version pays you interest for 10 years. The yield is the interest rate. When Treasury yields rise, it makes bonds attractive relative to riskier assets like Bitcoin.
The total dollar amount (or coin amount) traded in a given period. High volume = many trades; low volume = few trades. Helps measure how much activity an exchange or market had.
